narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 72.7% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a judgment of your worth or a guarantee of failure. The strongest reason was your third-year class rank: you were in the second decile, well below the roughly sixth-decile average among accepted students. This factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your first-year rank also pushed toward failure: third decile versus an accepted-student average around the sixth decile, though its influence was second. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.50 was above the accepted-student average of about 3.23, and this was the third-most influential factor; importantly, it pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the academic-rank concerns. To strengthen a future application, seek admissions feedback, consider additional rigorous coursework or a record-improving program, prepare carefully for a higher LSAT if you retake it, and document personal or professional growth. Reapply when your academic profile and test preparation give stronger evidence of bar readiness.
